lesson.title: Repeat it: loops
lesson.subtitle: Say it once, and how many times

video.title: Repeat it: loops: Say it once, and how many times
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Code is typed out on a card, left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph — the students’ computer studies teacher (main character)
Ms Amina Bello — the students’ teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.narration: My robot walked round the football pitch with sixteen cards. Forward, forward, forward, turn. Again and again! There must be a shorter way.
Look at the cards. Forward three times, then turn. The same four cards come again, four times. Steps that repeat make a pattern.
A loop tells the robot to repeat. Instead of laying the same card again and again, you lay it once and say how many times. Forward, three times.
Loops make programs shorter. They are easier to read. And if you want the robot to go further, you change just one number.
You know loops already. A clapping game repeats the same claps. A song repeats its chorus. Skipping a rope is a loop: jump, again and again.
Quick check! The robot has one card: forward, four times. How many squares does it move?
Four squares. One card, but it repeats four times. In the app, a card can repeat up to four times.
In the app, open Program a robot. Tap a card in your program to repeat it. Can you win three stars, with the fewest cards?
Your turn. Which program is shorter, but walks the same way: forward, forward, forward, or forward, three times?
Forward, three times. Remember: steps that repeat make a pattern. A loop repeats them for you. Loops make programs shorter and easier to change.
Try it yourself: make up a dance with a loop. Write it on paper, like step, step, clap, four times. Teach it to someone at home, using only your paper!

checkpoints.prompt: One card: forward, 4 times. How many squares does the robot move?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — one card, repeated four times: four squares.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — the card is one, but it repeats four times: four squares.

checkpoints.prompt: Which program is shorter, but walks the same way?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — one card that repeats is a loop: shorter, and it walks the same way.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — three cards against one card that repeats. The loop is shorter.
